transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. Well, I came in because... I just can't stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot right around my jaw and my neck. It really bothers me. Even when folks tell me it looks normal, I just can't let it go. I feel like it’s the very first thing the families I work with, or the nurses, or the people at my church notice when they look at me.
Do you find yourself repeatedly checking that area in mirrors or touching it over and over?

Yes, I do. Before I leave for work, or really any kind of meeting, I just... I keep going back to the bathroom mirror. I'll stand there fixing my collar, or adjusting my hair around my neck to try and cover it up. And then I'll take another look using my phone camera just to be sure. I also find myself asking my daughter if it looks strange to her. Honestly, doing all that has made me late more than once.
Do you believe that the spot around your jaw and neck really looks abnormal, despite other people telling you it looks normal?

Yes, I do. I mean... I know what everyone else says, but when I look in the mirror, it's just so obvious to me. It really does look abnormal. I just can't see it the way they do, no matter how many times they tell me it's fine.
At times, do you recognize that your worry about the way your jaw and neck look might be exaggerated or not really true?

No, not really. I mean... I guess I don't see it as exaggerated at all. To me, it's just exactly what I see when I look in the mirror. I don't really have moments where I think my worry isn't true or that I'm just making it up.
Has this concern about your jaw and neck caused problems in your daily life?

Yes, it definitely has. At work, I've actually passed up chances to help lead meetings or take on supervisory roles because... well, I just worry people will be staring right at my face and neck. And I've fallen behind on my paperwork a few times because I get stuck in the bathroom trying to make myself look presentable before I can even start my shift. Outside of work, I've stopped going to my book club and my walking group. Just the thought of getting ready and trying to hide it... it just feels like too much effort, so I stay home.
Are you mainly worried about how that area looks, rather than about it being a sign of a medical problem?
Yes, it's just about how it looks. I mean, I'm not worried that it's cancer or some kind of disease or anything like that. It's really just... the appearance of it. That's what bothers me so much.
Are you completely certain that your jaw and neck look abnormal?

Yes, I am completely certain. I mean, I see it every single day in the mirror. It's not something I'm imagining or blowing out of proportion. It just... it looks wrong, and I know it does. There's no doubt in my mind about it.
Besides looking in the mirror, do you do anything over and over to check, hide, or fix that area of your jaw or neck?

Yes, I do. Before I leave for work, or really any time I have to go out, I just keep going back into the bathroom. I'll stand there fixing my collar, pulling my hair around my neck to try and cover it up. And then... I'll take out my phone and use the camera to check it again. I also ask my daughter sometimes, just to see if she thinks it looks strange. Honestly, doing all that over and over has made me late more than once.
Do you have other unwanted thoughts that keep coming into your mind, besides worries about how your jaw and neck look?
No, not really. It's really just the jaw and neck thing. I don't have other thoughts like that getting stuck in my head.
When you check the mirror or adjust your hair and collar, is it mainly to deal with how your jaw and neck look?

Yes, exactly. It's all about trying to fix how my jaw and neck look. Like I said, I keep going back to the bathroom mirror before work, messing with my collar, pulling my hair around, checking my phone camera... and asking my daughter. It's all just to try and make that area look normal, or at least hide it so it's not so obvious. That's the only reason I do it, even when it makes me late.
Has any doctor ever told you that there is actually something wrong or abnormal with your jaw or neck?

No, no doctor has ever said anything like that. I mean, I've never been told there's an actual medical problem or anything physically wrong with my jaw or neck. It's just... well, it's just how it looks that bothers me so much. But no, medically, no one has ever said it's abnormal.
Is your main worry that your jaw and neck look ugly or deformed?

Yes, exactly. I mean, I came in today because I just can't stop seeing this sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. It just looks awful to me. Even when folks tell me it looks normal, I feel like it's deformed. I just know it's the first thing the families at work, the nurses, or even the people at my church notice when they look at me. It's just so ugly.
